title: Grow Your YouTube Channel & YagmanX
sourceLabel: HKDSE 2026 English Language Paper 1 Part B1 · Texts 2–3

paragraphs.label: Text 2 · 1

image.alt: Online Marketing Institute website header with About Us, eLessons, Articles, Online Store and Podcasts links
image.caption: Original website header from Text 2

paragraphs.text: YouTube is the world’s second-largest search engine after Google. For those of you with your own YouTube channel, YouTube can help people find the content on your channel quickly and drive engagement — if you know a few tricks. Here are some tips for you.

paragraphs.label: Text 2 · 2
paragraphs.text: Building your video around a single topic or keyword is a good way to drive traffic and grow your YouTube audience. To get the maximum number of viewers, use a keyword tool to look for the most searched keywords in the niche you want to target. Choose one, and then include it throughout your content so YouTube can pick it up when closed captions are added.

paragraphs.label: Text 2 · 3
paragraphs.text: Bear in mind that the most successful videos on YouTube are typically between one and five minutes long, so don’t feel you have to make a movie or write a novel. Keep them short and sweet.

paragraphs.label: Text 2 · 4
paragraphs.text: Of course, the best way to grow your YouTube channel is to create and distribute great content. But that content doesn’t always have to be built from scratch. Great videos can be created from what you already have. Review the blogs, guides, and other pieces you currently have and think about how to repurpose them to create relevant and engaging videos.

paragraphs.label: Text 2 · 5
paragraphs.text: YouTube is a social media platform and therefore demands social interaction. If you’re just posting videos without encouraging comments and discussion, you’re missing a trick. YouTube rewards channels with great engagement, including likes (and dislikes), and most importantly, comments. So try to respond to every comment you receive (if possible!)

paragraphs.label: Text 2 · 6
paragraphs.text: It can be extremely beneficial to personalise your channel by appearing in your videos. When you show your face, your audience can more easily connect with you. Not every video needs to include your face, but you should feature regularly enough to engage your audience.

paragraphs.label: Text 2 · 7
paragraphs.text: Finally, to grow your audience, you need to increase your posting frequency to at least one video a week. This may sound intimidating at first, but don’t worry; you don’t need a design firm or big advertising company to get this done as today’s smartphones offer excellent video recording ability. Consistency is of the utmost importance, so try to post at the same time each day or week (depending on your frequency), and keep your subscribers updated about when new videos will arrive. Then stick to your schedule.

paragraphs.label: Text 2 · 8
paragraphs.text: Follow these tips and see the results.

paragraphs.label: Text 3 · 1

image.alt: YagmanX YouTube video screenshot showing Yasmin Curren
image.caption: Original YagmanX screenshot from Text 3

paragraphs.text:
Yasmin Curren discusses how her YouTube channel, YagmanX, has impacted her life

When I started my YouTube channel, I didn’t expect much from it. It was just a hobby, something to do in my spare time. I was 19 and had been living in London for an internship, but I was lonely. I didn’t know anyone there — I had no friends and no money. Now I can look back and think that was a pretty good call. YouTube has completely transformed my life.

paragraphs.label: Text 3 · 2
paragraphs.text: Initially, I didn’t really see it as a career. As time went on though, my channel got more and more views and subscribers and I started to realise people were almost coming to depend on my videos. I knew I wanted to take YouTube more seriously, so I saved up and bought a high quality camera to make better videos.

paragraphs.label: Text 3 · 3
paragraphs.text: I’m now a computer games design student at university. You might wonder how I manage to balance all my university work with filming, editing, uploading and everything else being a YouTuber involves. For the most part I’ve got the right balance. I try and incorporate YouTube in everything I do. I’ve learnt to think ahead to work out how I can incorporate my university work into my YouTube channel.

paragraphs.label: Text 3 · 4
paragraphs.text: So, my YouTube channel and my progress as a student are quite merged, which makes things a lot easier. I’m going into my third year soon and for my final year project I’ll be developing a game over a whole year. I plan to update my viewers on my progress using videos and live streams. Having a relatively small but loyal base of subscribers means I can really get them involved.

paragraphs.label: Text 3 · 5
paragraphs.text: However, there have definitely been a few times I’ve struggled to get my assignments in on time because I’ve been too in the flow of making videos. I can’t help it. What I love most about being a YouTuber is the pure passion and adrenaline it makes me feel. I can be making fairly standard, sit-down, chatty videos one minute, and then the next thing I know I get an amazing idea out of nowhere, a flash of inspiration which I just HAVE to film right now. I find that buzz quite addictive.

paragraphs.label: Text 3 · 6
paragraphs.text: I’ve been told by my university lecturers that I could get a first if I really apply myself, but to me getting a first would probably mean being very good at doing what I’m told to do. Don’t get me wrong, I’m not a rebel. I see each assignment as an opportunity to get creative and see what I can do to push myself. I don’t really see it as a big deal if I miss out on getting a first because of YouTube — it means more to me to get a first for pushing boundaries, rather than doing what I know is easy. I don’t mind losing marks for taking risks and doing things in a slightly different way. Actually, my risk-taking approach paid off with one of my recent assignments. For three months I worked on a virtual reality game — it was hard work but I was determined to do it, and I got a first for that assignment.

paragraphs.label: Text 3 · 7
paragraphs.text: YouTube has also meant that I’ve managed to get myself out there in the public and test out ideas. I’d rather be working my hardest to stay networked online, to stay talking to companies, and to stay pushing my creativity and thinking outside the box, than to stifle it all and tick all the lecturers’ boxes to make sure I get a first.

paragraphs.label: Text 3 · 8
paragraphs.text: YouTube is about so much more than just becoming a famous YouTuber. I’ve been to a few secondary schools to explain how to use YouTube and social media to get that dream job. If you want to get started on YouTube, don’t worry about being perfect — show your viewers a bit of your personality, and then when you’ve got an audience, you’ve got people to give you global feedback, which is absolutely invaluable.

paragraphs.label: Text 3 · 9
paragraphs.text: So, go on. Give it a go. I know it’s scary and awkward at first to film yourself and put videos up there for potentially thousands of people to see, but trust me: it might be the best decision you’ve ever made.
